url.description: Echoed back from the input packet. apply_recheck compares it with the task's own inputs, so a rechecker that read a different page cannot have its answer applied to this one.

outcome.description: What happened when the page was fetched, judged by the agent rather than by an HTTP status code in our own client. `read` — the page came back and its text could be searched, so the per-quote verdicts below are meaningful. `blocked` — a login wall, a bot block, or a page that renders only under JavaScript; nothing can be judged, and every citation becomes `unverifiable`, which spec section 6 requires be flagged rather than silently trusted. `gone` — the page does not exist any more; every citation is rejected.

quotes.description: One verdict per quote in the input packet, addressed BY INDEX. Empty when `outcome` is not `read`. The quote text is deliberately not echoed: a model asked to repeat a long verbatim span will eventually retype it slightly wrong, and a mangled echo would be indistinguishable from a genuine absence. An integer cannot be mangled.

present.description: true only if this exact span appears in the page text. Not 'the page says something like this' — apply_recheck turns false into a rejected citation and drops the facts resting solely on it, so a generous reading here is how a fabricated quote reaches the report.

note.description: Free text, journaled. Where a rechecker says what it saw — 'the page now redirects to a paywall', 'the passage has been edited since'. Read by a human three days later, never parsed.
